limits.title: Races between writers of the `openfga` role driver (local roles)
limits.figure: persistent fail-open: 0 in ~38,800 interleavings of the in-memory double since the settle; against a real server not measured (M1); transient window: from a writer's `Write` to its own settle's correction
limits.where: `openfga`, `hierarchy: 'facts'`, local roles only; `database` has none (it decides on every question)
limits.effect: the five interleavings found by the F4 audit (`updateScopedRole`/`projectCatalogRole` ∥ `scopes.moved`; a `grant` that resolved the OLD chain; a `grant` during the relay lag of a unit ENTERING the owner; two INLINE `moved` of a parent and its child) no longer leave a binding edge outside the owner in the double: every writer of a local-role `scope#binding` re-reads with `HIGHER_CONSISTENCY` and corrects to a fixed point (the settle, 2.5.0-alpha.4). What remains declared is the window before that correction — a check in it can grant outside the owner, across tenants and past a deny of the owner — and the closing measurement against a real server
limits.recipe: serialise catalog writes with scope moves, keep the outbox, and run `authz:reconcile --to=openfga` after reorganising the tree
limits.detector: a non-zero exit of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` on a cron (`drift.roleVisibility`)
limits.closure: M1 (zero persistent fail-opens against a real server, with a positive control that turns red) is the exit criterion of experimental
limits.origin: README fila PROVISIONAL «Races between writers…» (F4, carreras 1–5; `backlog-2.6.md` §LOTE C carreras 1, 2, 4, 5); firma (lote C · carreras) (1): la ventana transitoria se acepta declarada; firma 3 de la estrategia: M1 deja de bloquear la RC

limits.title: Cost of a `moved`/`attached` of an existing scope with local roles (`openfga`)
limits.figure: 2 `Read`s per local role of the catalog per `moved`/`attached` (14 → 214 `Read`s with 100 local roles without a single binding, in the double; 2,008 with 1,000 in the F4 audit)
limits.effect: a tenant that defines many local roles slows the relay — one global queue — and widens the lag for everyone; zero `Read`s without local roles
limits.recipe: keep the number of local roles bounded and reorganise trees off-peak
limits.detector: the relay's lag: `authz:scopes:relay` reports `remaining: true` pass after pass
limits.closure: read the bindings per scope of the moved subtree (`scope:X#binding`) instead of per local role of the catalog
limits.origin: `backlog-2.6.md` §LOTE C carrera 6 (C1 del auditor F4); firma (lote C · carreras) (2): coste O(roles locales) declarado hasta 2.6

limits.title: Two concurrent `scopes.moved` of the SAME scope applied inline (`acceptScopeDriftRisk: true`, no outbox)
limits.figure: deterministic in the double (one preemption between the two movers); frequency against a real server not measured
limits.effect: the store keeps the parent of the writer that landed last, your tree the one that committed last: the store's tree diverges from yours and persists — a GLOBAL role skips the deny of the old tenant and an organisation role of the old tenant is inherited inside the new one
limits.recipe: use `scopes.outbox` (the relay applies your fresh parent), or lock the scope's row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) before `scopes.moved`
limits.detector: a non-zero exit of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` (its tree phase counts the divergent edge)
limits.closure: the `drift.treeMismatch` report and the `FOR UPDATE` recipe measured on PostgreSQL and MySQL
limits.origin: firma (lote C · TREE) (2): TREE en línea = 🟡 declarado bajo `acceptScopeDriftRisk`; juez TREE §5 regla 6 (control fijado en rojo)

limits.title: The store's tree diverging from yours WITH the outbox (two movers of the same scope, commit order ≠ relay order)
limits.figure: closed in code since 2.5.0-alpha.4 and in the in-memory double — the relay applies the consumer's FRESH parent; the closing measurement (S1/S5/R at 0 disagreements on PostgreSQL and MySQL, the `relay.trust-enqueued-parent` mutant at 1000/1000) not measured; before the fix, 1000/1000 forced and 8.5–11.5 % with natural concurrency
limits.where: `openfga`, `hierarchy: 'facts'` with `scopes.outbox`; SQLite does not suffer it (measured); `database` has none
limits.effect: if the fix does not hold under real concurrency, the same persistent divergence as the inline row, with every entry `applied`
limits.recipe: lock the scope's row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) before `scopes.moved`, and give the relay a resolver without a TTL cache
limits.detector: a non-zero exit of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` on a cron
limits.closure: S1/S5/R measured on PostgreSQL and MySQL, plus a property "everything through the outbox" (C1-6)
limits.origin: firma (lote C · TREE) (1) (🟠 que bloqueaba la RC; firma 3 de la estrategia la pasa a criterio de salida de experimental); `loteC-tree-medicion.md`; O-4/C1-6 (convergencia sin propiedad «todo por outbox»); firma (candado · preguntas) 1: el caso apunta al control existente (regla 7 de `visibility_settle.spec.ts` + mutante `relay.trust-enqueued-parent`)

limits.title: A cached resolver in the relay and two moves of the same scope within its TTL
limits.figure: deterministic with one stale cache entry; frequency not measured
limits.where: `openfga` with `scopes.outbox` (the fresh-parent relay is `hierarchyFacts` only); `database` has none
limits.effect: the relay applies the cached parent to both entries — the second as `consumer-parent`, "backed" by the first — and the store keeps the old parent while your tree has the new one, with nothing left in the queue to repair it
limits.recipe: give the relay's `scopes.resolveChain` no cache, or a TTL shorter than the time between two moves of one scope
limits.detector: `authz:scopes:relay` exits 1 with its `consumer-parent` line (`authz:scopes:requeue --apply` exits 0 with its own line)
limits.closure: the relay stops accepting a parent backed only by an entry of the same pass when the resolver may be cached
limits.origin: O-1 del re-ataque 1 (`loteC-asentar-fase2-reataque1.md`); firma (asentar · cierre 1): O-1 espera a la estrategia ⇒ declarar con (b)

limits.title: A scope restored with the same uuid after a `detached`, relayed by a resolver that answers `null`
limits.figure: deterministic; needs a blind resolver (filtered by tenant) and the reuse of a detached uuid; frequency not measured
limits.effect: the `attached` of the restored scope is applied as `superseded` with no edge: the scope exists in your tree and has no parent in the store, so it does not reach the root there (`rooted`) and denies everything on it, direct grants included (fail-closed) — while `database` grants
limits.recipe: do not reuse a detached scope's uuid, or notify `scopes.attached` again once the relay's resolver sees it
limits.detector: the `superseded` line of `authz:scopes:relay` (exit 0), and `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` (the missing edge)
limits.closure: a `superseded` backed only by an EARLIER `detached` of the same pass is refused instead
limits.origin: O-3 del re-ataque 1 (`loteC-asentar-fase2-reataque1.md`); efecto corregido en el cierre 1 del candado (🟡 2 del auditor: es fail-closed por `rooted`, no un bypass del deny)

limits.title: An orphan `assignee` after a `purgeRole` that ran out of rounds, resurrected by reusing the role's uuid
limits.figure: needs a failed purge (500 `E_AUTHZ_PURGE_INCOMPLETE`) with a concurrent writer, a fixed `CatalogRoleSpec.uuid` and a re-sync; frequency not measured
limits.effect: the retry of the purge does not see the concurrent writer's `assignee` (it enumerates by the `role_binding#role` anchor, already gone); if the role is declared again with the same uuid, that holder is a member again without any grant, and the first `grant` of the role on that scope makes it grant
limits.recipe: before declaring a role again with the same uuid, run `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` and, if it reports surplus facts, `--prune`
limits.detector: `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` counts it as `extra-fact` and exits non-zero
limits.closure: membership requires the `role_binding#role` anchor, and a `grant` that creates a binding's structure sweeps earlier `assignee`s
limits.origin: C2-1 (firma asentar · cierre 2 (a)) y R2-1 (firma asentar · cierre 3 = (A)); `loteC-asentar-fase2-cierre3.md` §4

limits.title: A `scope#binding` edge without `role_binding#role` after a failed purge racing a move (ORPHAN-edge)
limits.figure: 2 in 34,420 fault∥race interleavings of the double; it grants nothing
limits.effect: garbage that fails closed: an edge of a purged role that the purge's retry does not see
limits.detector: `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` counts it as `extra-fact` and exits non-zero
limits.closure: the purge enumerates the role's edges by `scope#binding` too, not only by the `role_binding#role` anchor

limits.title: Two concurrent projections of the same role (`updateScopedRole`/`projectCatalogRole`): a removed permission's `permits_*` survives
limits.figure: deterministic in the double (one preemption before the projection's read of the store); frequency against a real server not measured
limits.where: `openfga`, `hierarchy: 'facts'`; `database` has none (the catalog is its own table)
limits.effect: the projection that read the OLD catalog writes after the one that read the new one: the role keeps granting a permission the catalog no longer gives it, persistently — within the tenant that owns the role on this path (`updateScopedRole` is local roles only); the sync's projection is the same race on any role, global ones included, and is its own row (`openfga.catalog.permits-sync`)
limits.recipe: serialise catalog writes of one role, and run `authz:reconcile --to=openfga` after a burst of catalog changes
limits.detector: a non-zero exit of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` (its catalog phase counts the surplus `permits_*`)
limits.closure: after its `Write` the projection re-reads the catalog version fresh and re-projects to a fixed point
limits.origin: firma (lote C · TREE) (4) (i): el gemelo `permits_*`, sin medir; no entró en el paso 4 (`loteC-asentar-fase2-cierre3.md` «Lo que NO es mío»)

limits.title: The projection of `authz:catalog:sync` racing another catalog write: a removed permission's `permits_*` comes back
limits.figure: deterministic in the double (one preemption before the sync's projection reads the store); frequency not measured — the window grows with the catalog (one paged `Read` of `role:` per holder type after the commit)
limits.where: `openfga`, `hierarchy: 'facts'`; `database` has none (the catalog is its own table)
limits.effect: the sync takes its snapshot inside its transaction and projects after the commit without re-reading the version; if another write removes a permission in between (an `updateScopedRole`, or a second sync with another spec — a pod of the old release during a rolling deploy), the stale projection writes the `permits_*` back: the role keeps granting it, persistently, and with a GLOBAL role in every tenant where it is assigned; a real pass of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga` (the recipe itself) is the same race — it takes its catalog snapshot before it dumps the store, the freeze does not stop a sync, and a sync that removes a permission in between is reverted by the pass and reported as a write (it looks like a repair)
limits.recipe: do not run two `authz:catalog:sync` of different specs at the same time (one sync job per deploy), avoid catalog changes during a sync, and run `authz:reconcile --to=openfga` after a deploy has finished — never a real pass while a sync can run; check with `--dry-run` afterwards
limits.detector: a non-zero exit of `authz:reconcile --to=openfga --dry-run` (its catalog phase counts the surplus `permits_*`)
limits.closure: the sync's projection re-reads the catalog version after its `Write` and re-projects to a fixed point, like the twin's
limits.origin: 🟡 1 del auditor del candado (`loteRC-candado-auditor.md`): tercer escritor del gemelo `permits_*` (`src/catalog/catalog.ts` foto en la trx, `projectCatalog` tras el commit sin releer)

limits.title: `openfga:provision` publishes a model that narrows the reach of a live deny (a relation withdrawn from an `includes`)
limits.figure: deterministic (model and interpreter, no server): with `editor: { includes: ['owner'] }` and a live `denied_editor` on a direct owner, the owner is denied; narrowed to `includes: []`, `openfga:provision` publishes without refusing and the same tuples grant `owner`; how often a config narrows under live denies is not measured
limits.where: `openfga` (`openfga:provision`); `database` has the same residue through its own config store — the decision (8) guard there is a separate lot
limits.effect: the provision guard only refuses a model that DROPS a `denied_*` relation (`--allow-drop-deny`); narrowing an `includes` keeps every `denied_*` but shrinks what the deny cuts (the up-closure of D5), so a deny that blocked a holder stops blocking them, persistently, once the new model is pinned
limits.recipe: before narrowing or withdrawing a relation of a type with live denies, list them (`authz:relations:reconcile --dry-run` over the partitions, or `listDenies`) and re-issue each deny on the relation that still covers the access you mean to cut
limits.detector: none automatic: the model compares equal to the config (L11) and the reconcile sees no surplus tuple — review the config diff of every `includes` change against the live denies (a `--dry-run` listing of the denies whose reach shrank arrives before the RC, with the `database` half of decision (8))
limits.closure: the provision guard with the property «for every live deny, the new reach ⊇ the old reach» and an explicit forced way out (decision (8))
limits.origin: decisión (8) del dueño (2026-10-15 (8)) y H3 del auditor del plan RC (`loteRC-plan-auditor.md`); firma (candado · preguntas) 5: la mitad `openfga` se declara ya
